evidence: Plaut. Rud. 2.1.12: neque quicquam captum'st piscium (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of people taken in war (captī, captives) and of animals, birds and fish caught. A captive is captīvus (see prisoner).
Of a wanted person, a thief, a runaway: see arrest.
To lay hold of with the hand: a person by the arm, an animal by the scruff.

phrases.latin: mustēla ab homine prēnsa cum īnstantem necem effugere vellet: parce, quaesō, inquit, mihi
phrases.english: a weasel caught by a man, wanting to escape the death that was coming: “spare me, please,” she said

phrases.latin: vēnor aliquandō, sed nōn sine pugillāribus, ut quamvīs nihil cēperim nōn nihil referam
phrases.english: I hunt sometimes, but not without my notebooks, so that even if I catch nothing I bring something back
